headline: EU to legislate about Chat Control behind closed doors, activists warn of "double-attack"
summary: Civil rights activists warn of an unprecedented "double-attack" on secure messaging as EU meetings this week threaten mass surveillance and an end to anonymous communication. This move bypasses democratic processes.
details: Civil rights activist Dr. Patrick Breyer is sounding the alarm ahead of critical EU meetings this week. He warns of an unprecedented "double-attack" by European Parliament President Roberta Metsola and EU governments, threatening mass surveillance and an end to anonymous communication.

The first threat involves EP President Metsola's attempt to resurrect the expired "Chat Control 1.0" mass scanning regime. This move directly overrides the European Parliament's clear rejection of the proposal in March, which even her own EPP group opposed.

A recent leak reveals that the Council is meeting this Friday to try and adopt a first-reading position to force Chat Control 1.0 through. This is seen as a blatant disregard for democratic processes and fundamental rights.

Simultaneously, final trilogue negotiations on the permanent "Chat Control 2.0" regulation (2022/0155) will take place this Monday. The European Parliament is set to rush a new mandate on detection/scanning, potentially leading to fatal concessions in the trilogue with the Council.

In response to these imminent threats, civil society has updated and relaunched the campaign platform fightchatcontrol.eu. This platform enables citizens to immediately email EU lawmakers and government representatives, urging them to protect digital civil rights.

Dr. Breyer emphasizes that genuine child protection is possible without destroying the privacy of 450 million Europeans. He advocates for targeted, evidence-based investigations, security-by-design, and proactive deletion of material on the darknet, rather than error-prone algorithms that could criminalize innocent content.
caption:
EU lawmakers are pushing for 'Chat Control' legislation behind closed doors this week. Civil rights activists warn of an unprecedented 'double-attack' on secure messaging.

Civil rights activist Dr. Patrick Breyer is sounding the alarm ahead of critical EU meetings this week. He warns of an unprecedented "double-attack" by European Parliament President Roberta Metsola and EU governments, threatening mass surveillance and an end to anonymous communication.

The first threat involves EP President Metsola's attempt to resurrect the expired "Chat Control 1.0" mass scanning regime. This move directly overrides the European Parliament's clear rejection of the proposal in March, which even her own EPP group opposed.

A recent leak reveals that the Council is meeting this Friday to try and adopt a first-reading position to force Chat Control 1.0 through. This is seen as a blatant disregard for democratic processes and fundamental rights.

Simultaneously, final trilogue negotiations on the permanent "Chat Control 2.0" regulation (2022/0155) will take place this Monday. The European Parliament is set to rush a new mandate on detection/scanning, potentially leading to fatal concessions in the trilogue with the Council.

In response to these imminent threats, civil society has updated and relaunched the campaign platform fightchatcontrol.eu. This platform enables citizens to immediately email EU lawmakers and government representatives, urging them to protect digital civil rights.

Dr. Breyer emphasizes that genuine child protection is possible without destroying the privacy of 450 million Europeans. He advocates for targeted, evidence-based investigations, security-by-design, and proactive deletion of material on the darknet, rather than error-prone algorithms that could criminalize innocent content.
